paragraphs.text: Closes DeepSeek Harness runner processes that stay alive after their shell command finished, reclaim
ing ~140 MB each. Windows only.
# cg-shell-janitor

A DeepSeek Harness plugin for **Windows** that closes the runner processes DSH leaves behind
after a
shell command finished. Each one holds about 140 MB of RAM.
- Español
## The problem
On Windows every `dsh` shell call starts a private runner process:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

That runner owns the Win32 Job of the command. When the command ends the runner is supposed to
exit

on its own — its own `poll()` closes the empty Job and calls `finish(0)`. In practice it
often stays

alive: measured on DSH Desktop 0.2.x, eight of them had accumulated in a single
working session, 11
27 MB, the oldest one four and a half hours old and completely idle.

Neither `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local` nor `dsh-ops` exposes a shell lifetime setting, so
there
is nothing to configure. This plugin is the workaround.
## What it does

Every `intervalSeconds` it looks for DSH runner processes and closes the ones that are
provably doin

g nothing. Closing a runner releases its Win32 Job, which is the semantics DSH
already uses for its

osing a runner releases its Win32 Job, which is the semantics DSH
already uses for its own children.
It only acts when **all** of these hold:

1. The runner's parent is still the DSH host process.
2. The runner has no living child — its `bash.

exe` already exited.
3. None of the children it was ever seen with is still alive, so it is not baby

sitting a
background process. The tree is re-learned on every sample, so a command that left a serve

r
running behind `&` keeps its runner protected.
4. It is older than `idleMinutes`.
5. There are no

unattributable daemon-like orphans around. If there are, the plugin enters a
conservative mode and c
loses nothing that cycle.

The first sample after startup only observes, so the plugin learns the tree before deciding
anything
. Nothing is deleted, and no process is touched other than the leaked runner itself.
## Measured effect
Same machine, same session, right after the first real cycle:
| Metric | Before | After |

| Live runners | 8 (1127 MB) | 2 (288 MB, both with a live shell) |
| Free RAM | 3.37 GB | 5.78 GB |
| Total processes | 298 | 240 |
It closed three leaked runners and left the two that were running commands alone.
## Configuration
In `cordis.patch.yml`:
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `enabled` | `true` | turn the cycle off without uninstalling |
| `dryRun` | `false` | only log wha

t it would close |
| `intervalSeconds` | `180` | how often it samples (30–3600) |
| `idleMinutes` |

`5` | minimum age before closing (1–1440) |
| `reapOnStartup` | `true` | first sample 20 s after sta

minimum age before closing (1–1440) |
| `reapOnStartup` | `true` | first sample 20 s after startup |

A cycle costs about 2 seconds of one core every three minutes: it runs one `Get-CimInstance`
query t
hrough PowerShell. Raise `intervalSeconds` if that matters to you.
Log: `~/.dsh/shell-janitor.log`, rotated at 256 KB.
## Install
From the dsh-market catalog (one click), or from a local checkout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then restart the harness.

## Scope and limitations

- **Windows only.** The leak is in the Win32 Job-owning runner. On other platforms the plugin
logs o

ne line and does nothing.
- It is a heuristic, not a fix. The real fix belongs upstream: the runner

should exit by
itself.
- A runner created *before* the plugin loaded whose shell already exited has

no children on
record. It is still closed once it passes `idleMinutes`, because condition 5 only gua

rds
against orphans the plugin cannot attribute at all.
- If you deliberately keep a daemon alive fr

om a shell command and the plugin never observed
that command, the daemon is protected only by the c
onservative mode, not by an exact match.

# Español

Plugin para **DeepSeek Harness en Windows** que cierra los procesos runner que DSH deja vivos
despué
s de que su comando terminó. Cada uno ocupa unos 140 MB.

En Windows cada llamada a `dsh` crea un proceso runner que es dueño del Job de Win32 del
comando. Cu

ando el comando termina debería salir solo, pero muchas veces queda vivo: medido en
DSH Desktop 0.2.

x, en una sola sesión de trabajo se acumularon ocho, 1127 MB, el más viejo con
cuatro horas y media
de antigüedad y sin hacer nada.

Ni `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local` ni `dsh-ops` exponen un ajuste de vida del shell, así
que no
hay nada que configurar. Este plugin es el parche.

Cada `intervalSeconds` busca runners y cierra los que no están haciendo nada. Solo actúa si el
runne

r no tiene hijo vivo, no supervisa ningún proceso que se le haya conocido, es más viejo
que `idleMin

utes` y no hay huérfanos de tipo demonio que no sepa atribuir (si los hay, entra en
modo conservador
y no cierra nada). La primera muestra después de arrancar solo observa.

Log en `~/.dsh/shell-janitor.log`. Configuración en `cordis.patch.yml`. Solo Windows.
Licencia MIT.
